# dsh-voice

Martin's self-contained two-way voice plugin for the DSH web app: you speak,
the agent replies out l

oud, and the microphone keeps listening. Works on any
device the web app runs on (iPhone or PC).

A standalone fork of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-voice-input`
(0.1.7-rc.2, from the dee

pseek-harness checkout), renamed `@martindye/dsh-voice`
and grown into the single voice plugin: comp

oser in, speaker buttons and
auto-read out. The retired `dsh-voice-chat` kit and the old `dsh-voice-

output`
plugin are both superseded by this repository.
## What it does
Input (the composer):

- The unified 34 px blue composer button: voice entry on an empty draft, send
arrow while typing, st

op square while the agent runs or the system speaks,
cross while a voice turn is active.
- Continuou

s listening: after a reply ends the microphone reopens on its own;
an auto-open that draws no words

is quietly re-offered a few times.
- The spoken pause command ("hold the mic", "pause the mic", "sto

p
listening") parks the listening loop without sending.
- In-call mute: while a voice turn is active

the dictate button becomes a
mute/unmute toggle (white on red while muted); muted audio never reach

es
the recognizer and the voice-activity clocks freeze.
Output (the speaker):

- A speaker button on every finalized assistant message (speak / stop).
- Auto-read: fresh replies (

younger than 2 minutes) are read aloud on a
device that (1) has the auto-read toggle on and (2) has

used the voice
composer on that device (`dsh.voice-chat.v1`). No PC-side bridge is
involved — each d

evice reads what it is shown.
- A per-device auto-read toggle in the session header corner (green do

t when
the device is voice-armed), persisted per browser.
- Text is resolved from the session log on

the host and prepared for speech
(code, links and markdown stripped) before synthesis.
## Layout

- `src/` — plugin source. `src/index.ts` (host entry), `src/tts-host.ts`
(TTS supervision + speech p

reparation, host half), `src/client/` (browser
half: composer, speaker button, header toggle, playba

ck).
- `tts/` — the plugin's own TTS HTTP server (`server.py`) and its engines
(`qwen3.py` GPU voice

, `pocket.py` CPU fallback).
- `bin/tts-server.exe` — the bundled qwentts.cpp server for the qwen3 e

ngine
(adopts a compatible resident server on 127.0.0.1:8095 when present).
- `ref_voices/` — the re

ference voices the qwen3 engine clones from
(`pocket`, `warm-brit`). Both are synthetic takes (Pocke

t TTS and a
VoiceDesign take respectively) — no real person's voice is bundled; see
`THIRD-PARTY.md`

for the full attribution list.
- `lib/` — build output (`lib/index.js` node half, `lib/client.js` b

rowser
bundle). Gitignored; rebuild with `pnpm bundle`.
- `tests/` — vitest client tests (jsdom): th

e composer audio pipeline, the
waveform, and the conversation simulation with its trace files.
## Building
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The client bundle is a CJS closure factory registered with the host's module
loader under the packag

e name; platform modules (react, primitives, slots,
gateway) stay externals, everything else inlines

. CSS modules are compiled
with lightningcss and injected as self-managed style tags.
## Runtime requirements (the machine running DSH)

- Python 3 on PATH (override with `DSH_VOICE_PYTHON`) with `numpy` and
`requests`; add `pocket-tts`

for the CPU fallback engine. The server is
spawned on demand at `127.0.0.1:8189` (override the port

with
`DSH_VOICE_TTS_PORT`) and supervised by the plugin host.
- qwen3 (GPU) models under `~/.dsh/voi

ce-chat/models/qwen3` (talker +
tokenizer GGUFs); the engine choice is the shared consent file
`~/.d

sh/voice-chat/consent.json` (`"engine": "qwen3" | "pocket"`), default
qwen3 when its models are pres

ent.
- Host log: `~/.dsh/logs/voice-tts.log`.

With Pocket selected, only the CPU engine is warmed when the TTS server starts.
A failed Pocket requ

est does not fall back to a GPU engine. Selecting qwen3
still enables the GPU engine and retains its

CPU fallback. The host passes the
selected registry name through `VOICE_CHAT_PRELOAD_ENGINE`; a sta

ndalone server
or an older host defaults its warm-up to Pocket. GPU requests remain available
on dem

and. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_tts_server.py'`
for the model-free startup a

unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_tts_server.py'`
for the model-free startup and fallback checks.
## Installing

From npm (the published package ships prebuilt `lib/` — no build step, no
build-script permission ne

pm (the published package ships prebuilt `lib/` — no build step, no
build-script permission needed):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

for example `dsh plugin --profile web add @martindye/dsh-voice` for the web
app. Then restart the we

b host (or start it) and open the app: the unified
voice button appears in the composer, and a speak

er button on every finalized
message.

Requirements: DSH 0.1.7+ (web app), Node 22+ on the host, and Python 3 with
the TTS engine dependenc

ies for the spoken replies (see `tts/`); the browser
needs microphone permission for dictation, and

the speech-to-text models are
fetched on first use under the DSH home.
## How the bundle works

The package declares a `dsh.bundle` with `cordis.patch.yml`. Adding the
bundle to a profile's bundle

s list (the web profile does this in its
`package.json`) inserts:

- `ui-voice` — this plugin,
- the speech-to-text stack (`speech-to-text` with `sensevoice-local` as

default provider and language `en`, `speech-to-text-sensevoice` with
`dataRoot` at the DSH home `spe

ech-to-text/sensevoice`, and
`api-speech-to-text`),

and disables the upstream `ui-voice-input` row. The three `@deepseek-ai/
dsh-experimental-*speech-to

-text*` packages must be installed in the same
profile (the web profile links them from the deepseek

st be installed in the same
profile (the web profile links them from the deepseek-harness checkout).

`lib/` is not committed to git (it is included in the npm tarball); run
`pnpm bundle` after pulling

when working from a checkout. A page refresh
picks up the client; the host half needs a web-host res

working from a checkout. A page refresh
picks up the client; the host half needs a web-host restart.
